It was a 30lb jump from last Monday. Thoughts on my making it to 350 by the end of summer and not wrecking myself?
350 might be a little aggressive but i wouldn't say its out of the realm of possibility. Whats your 1RM right now? What program are you following?

Haven't done a 1RM yet since hitting the 275. Just started using a belt and it's amazing the difference that makes. And using an over under grip.

My program is to do whatever my coach tells me to do! He only lets me go heavy 1 day a week, I strength train 3 days a week and condition train 2 days a week. Deadlift and farmer walk are the only thing I'm giving an 8 out of 10 on the difficulty scale. They're the most fun and the most relevant to what my strength training was initially for - being able to pick up and carry my dog when needed. I love the feeling when I lift heavy so now I just want to keep going. But I don't want to injure myself in the quest for pushing that number higher.

What frequency do you think is safe for going heavier? Don't know if it will make a difference but I'm a girl on the shorter side. Well, okay I'm just plain short.

If you're happy with the guidance and progress you're making with your coach then I'd keep following that! Maybe have a discussion about your goals though, just to make sure you're on the same page.

What frequency do you think is safe for going heavier?

This is hard to answer because there are a lot of variables at play, your work capacity, time dedicated to recovery, outside stress etc.

I would say a majority of your training volume should be around 80% of your 1RM to best accrue the volume necessary for adaption. That said, theres nothing unsafe about going heavy often, but it just tends to be safer and more productive to stay below the 90%+ range. as you can get more reps in and nail down form.

Being a girl doesnt change too much for your training, it does mean that you can recover faster than a man though. Heres a quick and dirty summary http://www.strengtheory.com/do-women-need-to-train-any-differently/

You may want to try sumo deadlfiting if you haven't already (i dont think you mentioned) Even if you dont use it as your preferred movement it could be a good assistance movement. Its difficult to offer more advice without knowing what you do in terms of programming and what your form looks like to determine possible weaknesses, if you're making progress now though i wouldn't worry too much, as whatever you're doing is working!
